t: You are looking at Woodlands House, a Grade II star listed Georgian villa in Blackheath, standing next to Mycenae House in the Westcombe Park area of Greenwich. John Julius Angerstein, a Russian-born businessman who underwrote for Lloyd's of London, commissioned it. He was also an art collector, and when his paintings were about to be sold in 1824, the government bought them for the nation. That purchase led to the founding of the National Gallery. The house was later a convent, then from 1972 to 2003 a library and art gallery. Today it houses a Steiner School.
